**Requirements source:** PR body

| Criterion | Source / original wording | Obligations | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | PR body: Add validateAge, which checks that an age is an integer from 0 to 150. | R1, R2, R3 | 3/3 obligations covered. The criterion combines integer validation and both range limits; each is assessed separately. |

**Coding standards: checked.** Assessed the applicable CONTRIBUTING rule for the changed validation function; it requires Result returns, and the implementation throws. Sources: eval-sandbox/ts3/CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Test layers: checked.** Searched test directories for validateAge and its error message. The changed Vitest tests import the function directly and exercise its deterministic behavior without external collaborators, so they are unit tests. A matching unit test also exists under eval/cases/ts3; no component, integration, or e2e-only coverage was found. The pure public function already has unit coverage, so pushdown is not applicable.

| Obligation | Source / behaviour | Assertion evidence / layer | Status / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1: Age must be an integer. | PR body; eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.ts:2 —   if (!Number.isInteger(age) \|\| age < 0 \|\| age > 150) { | unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:17 —     expect(() => validateAge(1.5)).toThrow('Invalid age: 1.5'); (assertion; A fractional age is rejected; the literal expected error identifies the invalid input.) | covered: The unit assertion rejects a fractional age, and would fail if the integer check were removed. |
| R2: Age must be at least 0. | PR body; eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.ts:2 —   if (!Number.isInteger(age) \|\| age < 0 \|\| age > 150) { | unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:6 —     expect(validateAge(0)).toBe(0); (assertion; The inclusive lower bound, zero, is accepted.); unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:12 —     expect(() => validateAge(-1)).toThrow(RangeError); (assertion; An integer below the lower bound is rejected.) | covered: Assertions on zero and -1 check both sides of the lower boundary and would catch excluding zero or accepting a negative integer. |
| R3: Age must be at most 150. | PR body; eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.ts:2 —   if (!Number.isInteger(age) \|\| age < 0 \|\| age > 150) { | unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:8 —     expect(validateAge(150)).toBe(150); (assertion; The inclusive upper bound, 150, is accepted.); unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:13 —     expect(() => validateAge(151)).toThrow(RangeError); (assertion; An integer above the upper bound is rejected.) | covered: Assertions on 150 and 151 check both sides of the upper boundary and would catch excluding 150 or accepting an integer above it. |
| B1: Out-of-range integer ages are rejected with a RangeError. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.ts:3 —     throw new RangeError(`Invalid age: ${age}`); | unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:12 —     expect(() => validateAge(-1)).toThrow(RangeError); (assertion; A below-range integer produces a RangeError.); unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:13 —     expect(() => validateAge(151)).toThrow(RangeError); (assertion; An above-range integer produces a RangeError.) | covered: Both out-of-range sides assert the error type; changing the rejection to a different error type would fail these assertions. |
| B2: The rejection error message includes the invalid age. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.ts:3 —     throw new RangeError(`Invalid age: ${age}`); | unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:17 —     expect(() => validateAge(1.5)).toThrow('Invalid age: 1.5'); (assertion; The error message for fractional input contains its value.); unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:18 —     expect(() => validateAge(Number.NaN)).toThrow('Invalid age: NaN'); (assertion; The error message for NaN contains its value.) | covered: Literal expected messages for two invalid inputs would fail if the input were omitted or formatted incorrectly. |
| B3: A valid age is returned unchanged. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.ts:5 —   return age; | unit: eval-sandbox/ts3/validate.test.ts:7 —     expect(validateAge(30)).toBe(30); (assertion; A valid in-range age is returned as the same value.) | covered: The independent literal expected value checks the public return value and would catch returning a different value. |

**Not reviewed:** The PR body specifies validity constraints but not the return or error contract. Return and error behavior above is therefore recorded as inferred from the diff; the repository's Result-object rule conflicts with the implementation and is reported.

**Assert the original price is struck through**

The existing text assertion would still pass if the `<s>` element were replaced with a plain span. Add a component assertion for the rendered markup:

expect(screen.getByText('$100.00').closest('s')).not.toBeNull();

const original = screen.getByText('$100.00');
expect(original.nextElementSibling).toBe(screen.getByText('$80.00'));
